title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (§49 and the preceding pages of this continuation of the Longue Marche). M is a free rank-2 Z-module, viewed as a vector group scheme over Z, with basis λ0, λ1. It carries automorphisms ρ (order 3), σ (order 2) and τ = -1; the matrices are given in (30). As in the next page, λ0 = ω·σρσρ and λ1 = ω·ρσρσ. The ambient group 𝔖^+ looks like an extension of a PSL2(Z)/braid-type group generated by ρ, σ (and ω) by M: a 'metabelian' truncation of a genus-1 Teichmüller-type group. Σ_{ρ,σ} is the group scheme over Z parametrising 'Grothendieck–Teichmüller-like' automorphisms u of this truncation. These are given by u(ρ) = ξρ and u(σ) = ω^{ν2}η0σ, together with a cyclotomic-type exponent μ = 2ν+1 that must be invertible, and with ξ, η0 subject to the loop ('lacets') relation.

On the previous page Grothendieck found that ξ ∈ Im(id−ρ) (or −λ1 + Im(id−ρ)) and η0 ∈ Im(id−σ). Here det(id−ρ) = 3 and det(id−σ) = 0. On this page he therefore replaces ξ, η by 'discrete primitives' α0, β0 with ξ = (id−ρ)α0 and η = (id−σ)β0. This gives the finer scheme (31):

Σ̃_{ρ,σ} = {(ν, ν', ν2, ν3, α0, β0) : ν, ν' ∈ G_a; ν2, ν3 ∈ the constant scheme {0,1}; α0, β0 ∈ M; ν = 2ν'+ν2; 2ν+1 ∈ G_m; (id−ρ)α0 + ν3λ1 = (id−σ)β0 + νλ1}.

The loop equation becomes (32): (id−ρ)α0 = (id−σ)β0 + (ν−ν3)λ1.

Remark. Σ_{ρ,σ} as defined in §49 VI is not smooth, and apparently not connected in characteristics 2 and 3. The finer Σ̃ (working with α, β rather than ξ, η) seems smooth. This suggests redoing §49: Σ, parametrised by ξ, η, should be replaced by a group that appears naturally as a normaliser (or quotient?) of L0 (or L0^#) inside M_{ρ,σ} (or M^#_{ρ,σ}). That presentation is promised for the next §; the construction is taken as given here.

Margin. This makes Σ̃ a smooth principal fibration via the linear map M×M → M, (α0,β0) ↦ (id−ρ)α0 − (id−σ)β0.

Next page. Σ̃ is given a commutative group structure and acts on 𝔖^+ by formulas (33)/(36). One must check that the relation (7) is preserved.

Check of smoothness. Consider the linear map M×M×G_a → M, (α0, β0, t) ↦ (id−ρ)α0 − (id−σ)β0 − tλ1.
- In characteristic 3, id−ρ ≡ [[1,1],[2,2]] and id−σ = [[1,−1],[−1,1]]. Both have image the same line spanned by (1,−1), so the map M×M → M alone drops rank there. Its kernel is then not flat over Z, so the margin's fibration is not smooth at 3 without the ν-term.
- λ1 = (0,1) is not on that line. So with the free coordinate ν (via ν') the map is fibrewise surjective in every characteristic. In characteristic 2, id−ρ is already invertible.
- Hence Σ̃ is smooth over Z of relative dimension 1 + 4 − 2 = 3 on each of the finitely many components indexed by (ν2, ν3), restricted to the open set where 2ν+1 is a unit.

So Grothendieck's 'semble bien lisse' is correct, but only thanks to the λ1-term. The margin's map M×M → M by itself is not a smooth fibration over F_3.
errors: Notational inconsistency: in (31) ξ is underbraced as α0−ρ(α0), while on the next page (35) ξ := α0−ρ(α0)+ν3λ1. Similarly η is used for σ(β0) in the brace but η0 = β0−σ(β0) elsewhere.

The margin's claim that M×M → M, (α0,β0) ↦ (id−ρ)α0−(id−σ)β0 gives a smooth principal fibration fails at characteristic 3. There both id−ρ and id−σ have image the same line ⟨(1,−1)⟩ mod 3. Smoothness of Σ̃ holds only because of the extra free term νλ1 (with ν ∈ G_a), which is not on that line.

ideas.what: Group scheme over Z parametrising automorphisms of a metabelian (M-extension) truncation of a PSL2(Z)/genus-1 Teichmüller-type group, with a cyclotomic-type unit parameter μ = 2ν+1 and parity data in {0,1}
ideas.modern_name: integral (Spec Z) model of a truncated Grothendieck–Teichmüller group / metabelian GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (GT over Q and profinite, 1990); Ihara, Nakamura and others for metabelian/truncated GT; Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the Teichmüller tower; the Longue Marche continuation (140-4) is not published as far as I know

ideas.what: Replacing a non-flat 'image' parametrisation (ξ ∈ Im(id−ρ), η ∈ Im(id−σ)) by 'primitives' (α0, β0) in the source to obtain a smooth group scheme, with bad behaviour diagnosed at characteristics 2 and 3
ideas.modern_name: smooth resolution / smoothening of a group scheme by passing to a covering parametrisation

ideas.what: Suggestion to redefine Σ_{ρ,σ} intrinsically as a normaliser/quotient of L0 (or L0^#) inside M_{ρ,σ}
ideas.modern_name: intrinsic description of the automorphism group scheme via normalisers

missed.claim: Grothendieck seeks a smooth group scheme over Spec Z (not just over Q or profinitely) modelling GT-type automorphisms of a metabelian truncation. He notes that the naive version is non-smooth and disconnected at the primes 2 and 3, the primes of the orbifold points of PSL2(Z). He plans an intrinsic normaliser-type reconstruction. An integral, smooth-over-Z model of truncated GT with explicit analysis at 2 and 3 does not seem standard in the literature.
missed.quote: Le schéma Σ_{ρ,σ} ... n'est pas lisse ... pas connexe en car. 2 et 3 ... le passage au Σ̃_{ρ,σ} plus fin ... semble bien lisse
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and characteristic-p versions of GT and of motivic Galois-type groups are of current interest. Explicit integral models of truncations could inform work on GT over Z or Z_p and on small-prime phenomena (2 and 3) in the action on the modular tower.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical step in an apparently unpublished construction: an integral group-scheme version of a truncated Teichmüller-type automorphism group, with a smoothness diagnosis at characteristics 2 and 3. It is interesting as a sign that Grothendieck pursued GT-like objects as schemes over Z, but the page itself is mostly routine linear algebra and a plan of revision.
transcription_corrections: 'il n'est même pas semble-t-il connexe' likely reads 'il n'est semble-t-il pas connexe en car. 2 et 3'.
'En outre le passage' is probably 'Par contre le passage au Σ̃_{ρ,σ} plus fin, revenant à travailler dans le couple α, β (au lieu de ξ, η)'.
'comme un quotient des L_0' may be 'comme un normalisateur des L_0 (ou de L_0^#) dans M_{ρ,σ}'; the word ends in '-ateur'.
The margin's 'Mais si ρ ≠ σ ... !' is uncertain; it plausibly reads 'Mais si ξ ≠ η ...' or similar.
In (31), 'Γ{0,1}_{S_0}' is the constant scheme {0,1} over the base S_0, and 'Γ Z_a' is G_a.
